title: Seventy miles an hour 时速70英里
description: A dialogue lesson in which a policeman stops a man named Gary for driving too fast. The story introduces the modal verbs for past deduction 'must have been driving' (past continuous) and 'can't have been', and the structure 'you'd better (not) do something' for strong advice. The dialogue runs through Ann warning Gary to drive slowly, the policeman stopping him, Gary claiming he can't have been driving that fast, and the policeman warning him not to do it again. The workbook drills comprehension of the dialogue and vocabulary fill-in; the grammar workbook completes sentences with 'must have' or 'can't have' past forms, agrees with 'you'd better' advice, and completes advice with 'had better'.
answer_note: The dialogue is the lesson text. The comprehension questions (workbook A) and vocabulary fill-in (workbook B) are from the workbook answer key (source-key, img/key-123-129.jpg p.215 and img/key-129-135.jpg p.216). Grammar I (complete with must have / can't have past forms), II (agree with you'd better) and III (complete with had better) are from the grammar workbook answer key (source-key, pdf p.565).

lesson.text: Listen to the tape then answer this question. What does Ann advise her husband to do next time? 听录音，然后回答问题。安建议她的丈夫下次做什么？
lesson.translation: 听录音，然后回答问题。安建议她的丈夫下次做什么？

lines.speaker: ANN
lines.text: Look, Gary! That policeman's waving to you. He wants you to stop.
lines.translation: 瞧，加里！那个警察正朝你挥手呢。他要你停下来。

lines.speaker: POLICEMAN
lines.text: Where do you think you are? On a race track? You must have been driving at seventy miles an hour.
lines.translation: 你认为你现在是在哪儿？在赛车道上吗？你刚才一定是以每小时70英里的速度开车。

lines.speaker: POLICEMAN
lines.text: I was doing eighty when I overtook you.
lines.translation: 我是以每小时80英里的速度赶上你的。

lines.speaker: POLICEMAN
lines.text: Didn't you see the speed limit?
lines.translation: 难道你没看见限速牌吗？

lines.speaker: GARY
lines.text: I'm afraid I didn't, officer. I must have been dreaming.
lines.translation: 恐怕我没有看见，警官。我一定是思想开小差了。

lines.speaker: ANN
lines.text: He wasn't dreaming, officer. I was telling him to drive slowly.
lines.translation: 警官，他思想没有开小差。我刚才正告诉他开慢点。

lines.speaker: GARY
lines.text: That's why I didn't see the sign.
lines.translation: 所以我才没看见那牌子。

lines.speaker: POLICEMAN
lines.text: Let me see your driving licence.
lines.translation: 让我看一看你的驾驶执照。

lines.speaker: POLICEMAN
lines.text: I won't charge you this time. But you'd better not do it again!
lines.translation: 这次我就不罚你款了。但你最好不要开再这样快。

lines.speaker: GARY
lines.text: Thank you. I'll certainly be more careful.
lines.translation: 谢谢您。我以后一定会多加注意。

lines.speaker: ANN
lines.text: I told you to drive slowly, Gary.
lines.translation: 加里，我刚才叫你开慢点吧。

lines.speaker: GARY
lines.text: You always tell me to drive slowly, darling.
lines.translation: 你总是叫我开慢点，亲爱的。

lines.speaker: ANN
lines.text: Well, next time you'd better take my advice!
lines.translation: 好啦，下次你最好还是听从我的劝告吧！

items.title: 1. Where do you think you are?
items.text: do you think 是用在特殊疑问句中的插入语，用来征询见解或表达看法。

items.title: 2. must have been driving
items.text: 这种结构用来表示对过去正在进行的事情的推测。可译为「一定」或「准是」。

items.title: 4. I was doing eighty when I overtook you.
items.text: 其中的动词 do 表示「以……速度行进」。

items.title: 5. But you'd better not do it again!
items.text: you'd better = you had better，后面加动词原形。had better 用于建议在将来某一具体场合采取动作，而不用於一般情况，比 should 语气更为强烈，常有威胁、告诫或催促的意味。

items.title: 6. you'd better take my advice!
items.text: 你最好还是听从我的劝告。take one's advice 是「听从劝告」的意思。

practice.title: Practice A: Comprehension
practice.instruction: Look at the dialogue on Students' Book page 261 and answer these questions. 参见学生用书第261页上的对话，然后回答以下问题。
practice.translation: 参见学生用书第261页上的对话，然后回答以下问题。
practice.key_source: img/key-123-129.jpg p.215 and img/key-129-135.jpg p.216 (Lesson 129 A)

questions.prompt: Who is waving at Gary?
questions.answer: A policeman (is waving at him).

questions.prompt: What does he want Gary to do?
questions.answer: He wants Gary to stop.

questions.prompt: What does the policeman say to Gary about his speed? ('You ...')
questions.answer: 'You must have been driving at seventy miles an hour.'

questions.prompt: How does Gary disagree? What does he say?
questions.answer: 'I can't have been.'

questions.prompt: Did the policeman overtake Gary?
questions.answer: Yes, he did.

questions.prompt: What speed was he doing?
questions.answer: He was doing eighty.

questions.prompt: Did Gary see the speed limit?
questions.answer: No, he didn't.

questions.prompt: What does Gary say about dreaming?
questions.answer: 'I must have been dreaming.'

questions.prompt: What was Ann telling Gary to do?
questions.answer: She was telling him to drive slowly.

questions.prompt: The policeman wants to see Gary's driving licence. How does he ask him?
questions.answer: (He says:) 'Let me see your driving licence.'

questions.prompt: How does the policeman warn Gary not to do it again?
questions.answer: 'But you'd better not do it again.'

questions.prompt: Does Gary promise to be more careful? What does he say?
questions.answer: Yes, he does. (He says:) 'I'll certainly be more careful.'

practice.title: Practice B: Vocabulary
practice.instruction: Fill in the missing word or words in these sentences. They all come from the dialogue. 根据对话填空。
practice.context: 5 fill-in-the-blank vocabulary items drawn from the dialogue.

questions.prompt: The big car was going too fast for me to ___ it.
questions.answer: overtake

questions.prompt: The ___ ___ in the town is only thirty miles an hour.
questions.answer: speed limit

questions.prompt: 'Didn't you see the "SLOW" ___?' said the policeman when he stopped me.
questions.answer: sign

questions.prompt: A policeman stopped Kate and asked to see her ___ ___.
questions.answer: driving licence

questions.prompt: You must drive more slowly on this road. It's not a race ___ , you know!
questions.answer: track

grammar.title: Grammar I: Rewrite the sentences using 'must have been/done' or 'can't have been/done'
grammar.instruction: 仿照例句用 must have been/done 或 can't have been/done 改写下列句子。
grammar.translation: 仿照例句用 must have been/done 或 can't have been/done 改写下列句子。
grammar.key_source: pdf p.565 (新概念英语语法练习1)
grammar.context: 10 rewrite items; item 1 (In my opinion, you didn't see me. I wasn't there. → You can't have seen me. I wasn't there.) is the printed example. The key gives the rewritten clause for each item.

questions.prompt: In my opinion, you didn't see me. I wasn't there.
questions.answer: You can't have seen me. I wasn't there.

questions.prompt: I'm sure you had a good time yesterday. You all looked excited.
questions.answer: You must have had a good time yesterday. You all looked excited.

questions.prompt: The men worked all day without a rest. I am sure they were very tired.
questions.answer: The men worked all day without a rest. They must have been very tired.

questions.prompt: I don't think you did all that by yourself. It was not easy.
questions.answer: You can't have done all that by yourself. It was not easy.

questions.prompt: That peach tasted unpleasant. I'm sure it was bad.
questions.answer: That peach tasted unpleasant. It must have been bad.

questions.prompt: I'm sure he wasn't there because I didn't see him.
questions.answer: He can't have been there because I didn't see him.

questions.prompt: I'm sure you didn't pass the exam. You didn't study for it.
questions.answer: You can't have passed the exam. You didn't study for it.

questions.prompt: I'm sure that it didn't rain last night. The ground is not wet.
questions.answer: It can't have rained last night. The ground is not wet.

questions.prompt: You didn't go anywhere after dinner in the restaurant. I'm sure you left your case there.
questions.answer: You didn't go anywhere after dinner in the restaurant. You must have left your case there.

questions.prompt: I'm sure you ate my biscuits. Why didn't you tell me?
questions.answer: You must have eaten my biscuits. Why didn't you tell me?

grammar.title: Grammar II: Answer the questions using 'had better do'
grammar.instruction: 仿照例句用 had better do 回答下列问题，并做必要的改变。
grammar.translation: 仿照例句用 had better do 回答下列问题，并做必要的改变。
grammar.key_source: pdf p.565 (新概念英语语法练习1)
grammar.context: 10 answer items; item 1 (Do I have to change my shirt? → Yes, you'd better change your shirt.) is the printed example.

questions.prompt: Do I have to change my shirt?
questions.answer: Yes, you'd better change your shirt.

questions.prompt: Do I have to have a bath?
questions.answer: Yes, you'd better have a bath.

questions.prompt: Does he have to have a haircut?
questions.answer: Yes, he'd better have a haircut.

questions.prompt: Do we have to get something to eat?
questions.answer: Yes, we'd better get something to eat.

questions.prompt: Do I have to do my homework?
questions.answer: Yes, you'd better do your homework.

questions.prompt: Does she have to go and see a doctor?
questions.answer: Yes, she'd better go and see a doctor.

questions.prompt: Do I have to telephone the teacher?
questions.answer: Yes, you'd better telephone the teacher.

questions.prompt: Does he have to take his son to school?
questions.answer: Yes, he'd better take his son to school.

questions.prompt: Do I have to do some shopping?
questions.answer: Yes, you'd better do some shopping.

questions.prompt: Does she have to water the flowers?
questions.answer: Yes, she'd better water the flowers.

grammar.title: Grammar III: Give advice using 'had better (not) do'
grammar.instruction: 仿照例句用 had better (not) do 写出下列各句的对应句。
grammar.translation: 仿照例句用 had better (not) do 写出下列各句的对应句。
grammar.key_source: pdf p.565 (新概念英语语法练习1) for items 3-7; items 8-12 are model answers
grammar.context: 12 advice items; items 1 and 2 are the printed examples. The answer key prints only items 3-7; items 8-12 have no printed key, so their answers are model answers (suggested).

questions.prompt: I feel sleepy. (get some sleep)
questions.answer: You'd better get some sleep.

questions.prompt: I've got a bad cold. (not go swimming)
questions.answer: You'd better not go swimming.

questions.prompt: He's got a headache. (take an aspirin)
questions.answer: He'd better take an aspirin.

questions.prompt: I'm very tired. (not stay up late)
questions.answer: You'd better not stay up late.

questions.prompt: I'm not feeling well tonight. (not go out)
questions.answer: You'd better not go out.

questions.prompt: The bus is crowded. (take a taxi)
questions.answer: You'd better take a taxi.

questions.prompt: She feels hot. (open the windows)
questions.answer: She'd better open the windows.

questions.prompt: It's raining today. (stay in)
questions.answer: You'd better stay in.

questions.prompt: The baby is sleeping. (not turn on the stereo)
questions.answer: You'd better not turn on the stereo.

questions.prompt: She's got a temperature. (not eat too much)
questions.answer: She'd better not eat too much.

questions.prompt: I don't understand the text. (ask your teacher)
questions.answer: You'd better ask your teacher.

questions.prompt: He has got a stomachache. (not drink anything)
questions.answer: He'd better not drink anything.
